copies.headline: John's Tight Ends Outgun Noah's Backfield
copies.body:
The gap here is at tight end and the top of the receiver room. John can start Brock Bowers (16) and still leave Trey McBride (14) on his bench, while Noah's best tight end is rookie Colston Loveland at 12 with Brenton Strange behind him. Add Puka Nacua's 21 in a Rams-Niners game with a 48.5 total — the highest on the board — and John's ceiling is simply higher. Noah's counterpunch is real but narrow: De'Von Achane (18) and James Cook (15) give him a seven-point edge at running back, except Achane's Dolphins are 3.5-point dogs in a 40.5-point game, the ugliest environment on the slate.
The swing factor is Nacua's questionable tag, and it's the whole game. Without him John's receiver group thins to Quentin Johnston and Brian Thomas Jr. Noah's wideouts aren't much better — Mike Evans and Josh Downs are both dinged, and Garrett Wilson sits in a 38.5-total game. John's the worse team on paper at #11; this week the matchups don't care.

copies.headline: Isaac's Receiver Room Is One Big Injury Report
copies.body:
The projections say a one-point game, which is the fantasy equivalent of a coin flip, but the tags break the tie. Isaac's top three receivers — Ja'Marr Chase, Malik Nabers, DK Metcalf — are all questionable, as are Wan'Dale Robinson and Jakobi Meyers, so his one clear positional edge (46 to 41 on the best three) is also the one most likely to evaporate by Sunday morning. Terry McLaurin and Adonai Mitchell are the safety net, and that's not a net. Chase in a 50.5-point game against Tampa is the ceiling; without him, Isaac is starting a WR3 he didn't plan on.
Kaleb's advantages are structural. Justin Herbert as a 10.5-point home favorite is the steadiest QB here — Bo Nix travels to Kansas City in a 42.5-point game with the lowest total on the slate. Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall carry their own tags, but RB is the deeper room, Harold Fannin beats Hockenson, and Kaleb needs less to go right.

copies.headline: Two Bad Rosters, One Reluctant Winner
copies.body:
This is the 9-versus-10 game and it looks like it, with a two-point projection gap decided almost entirely at receiver. Grant's top three (Amon-Ra St. Brown 19, Zay Flowers 14, Jaylen Waddle 12) beat CJ's by six, and St. Brown gets the best environment on the slate — Detroit favored by seven with a 49.5 total, New Orleans throwing from behind all afternoon. CJ counters with Joe Burrow (18) in a 50.5-point game against Tampa, the highest total on the board, which is the cleanest edge either team has. Running backs are a dead heat: Omarion Hampton (18) against Arizona as a 10.5-point favorite versus Jonathan Taylor (18) as a home underdog.
CJ's problem is the questionable tags stacked behind everything. Emeka Egbuka, Alec Pierce, Chuba Hubbard and TreVeyon Henderson are all uncertain, with Pacheco on IR and Charbonnet out, so the RB depth is theoretical. If Egbuka and Pierce both sit, Parker Washington and Ja'Kobi Lane are starting, and that's a 20-point receiver room. Grant has Flowers questionable too but Christian Watson and Chris Godwin behind him. Burrow's ceiling keeps this close; Grant's floor wins it.

copies.headline: Logan's Eagles Stack Outruns Adam's Depth
copies.body:
The math is simple and it lives in Philadelphia. Logan runs Jalen Hurts (21) and Saquon Barkley (18) out of the same 45.5-total game where the Eagles are favored by 5.5 — the exact script where Hurts vultures a goal-line score and Barkley closes it out on the ground. Adam counters with Jayden Daniels (17) on the losing end of that same game, which at least means garbage-time volume, but he's giving up four at quarterback and five at running back with Kenneth Walker III stuck in a 42.5-total slog against Denver. Rico Dowdle and Bucky Irving at 12 apiece is fine depth, not a fix.
Adam's edge is receiver, and it's only two points: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Chris Olave chasing a 49.5 in Detroit as a seven-point dog, Rome Odunze. Sam LaPorta questionable at tight end is the real crack — Mark Andrews at 10 softens it. Logan has five questionable receivers, which sounds worse than it is when four of them are interchangeable.

copies.headline: Peter's Tight End Depth Is One Guy
copies.body:
Three points separate the #2 and #3 power rankings, and the tiebreaker is health. Christian's edge is receiver volume: CeeDee Lamb in a 48.5-total game the Cowboys are barely favored in, DeVonta Smith against Washington, and Jameson Williams as the third option in a Lions game with a 49.5 total. Peter counters with George Pickens (same Dallas game, so he's stacking that shootout) and A.J. Brown, but Tee Higgins is questionable and the Bengals-Bucs 50.5 is the fattest total on the board — if Higgins sits, Peter's WR3 falls to Denzel Boston at 8.
Peter wins quarterback with Lamar Jackson, who has Indianapolis and a 48.5 total, and Bijan Robinson gets chase-mode volume as a 3.5-point dog in Pittsburgh. But Tucker Kraft is Peter's only tight end and he's tagged; Christian at least has Chig Okonkwo behind a questionable George Kittle. Christian's running back room also survives a Bhayshul Tuten scratch — Chase Brown, Travis Etienne and Aaron Jones is four deep. Peter's ceiling is higher. His floor is a hole.

copies.headline: One Point Apart, Two Injury Reports Deep
copies.body:
Leif projects ahead by a single point, which means this comes down to whose questionable tags clear. Christian McCaffrey (18) in a 48.5-total game at the Rams is the swing on both ends — if he sits, Derrick Henry (16), David Montgomery (13) and Woody Marks fill in fine, but Leif's 35-point running back edge evaporates fast. Josh Allen at Houston in a 44.5 total is the low-ceiling version of a great quarterback, and Mitchell's Jaxson Dart is a 2.5-point home underdog against Dallas in a 48.5 — that's a lot of fourth-quarter throwing for an 18-point projection.
Mitchell's advantage is receiver, and it's real: Nico Collins, Courtland Sutton and DJ Moore for 39 against Leif's 36, with Marvin Harrison Jr. and Jayden Reed both volatile. But Mitchell's backfield behind Jahmyr Gibbs is rubble — Rachaad White questionable, Josh Jacobs day-to-day, Kaleb Johnson projecting one point. Gibbs against New Orleans keeps him alive; a Detroit blowout where Detroit sits on it doesn't.

intro: Leif over Mitchell by 0.7 is the closest line on the board, with Kaleb-Isaac (1.4) not far behind — four of the six games project inside three points, which is another way of saying nobody's roster has separated from anybody else's yet. The exception is John, favored by 8.8 over Noah, the widest gap of the week and the only matchup where the projections have picked a side with any conviction. Nothing's at stake in the standings, which means every one of these is purely about who has to hear about it until Sunday.
